context:
Goal: you answer from one place without retyping options.
Problem (rule): R18 (2026-11-10 16:46 CST) says chat holds one line, "on the page, item N". Main's guard option-labels-match-chat enforces `Page item: <id>` plus `a) <label>` lines, from your 2026-11-08 12:35 CST words "A and B mean the same". #3006 follows R18 and fights that guard.
Based on (ruling): R18; decision option-keys-are-letters.
Departs from: main — main keeps the option lines; choosing b drops them.
Meanwhile: #3006 holds until you answer.
home: rulings R18 and R60; guard option-labels-match-chat

options.gain: The guard keeps working; chat shows what you pick between.
options.how: Keep `Page item: <id>` and the `a) <label>` lines; #3006 is rebuilt to match.
options.label: Page item plus option lines (triage's pick; main today)
options.lose: Chat is longer: about one line per option in every reply that holds options (15 to 30 words each, unmeasured), so more tokens.

options.gain: Shortest chat; the tokens a saves.
options.how: Chat carries one line; the guard option-labels-match-chat changes with #3006.
options.label: One line, 'on the page, item N' (R18)
options.lose: No options in chat to compare against the page; a mismatch would go unnoticed.

reply: Yes, a costs tokens. A reply that holds options repeats one line per option in chat, about 15 to 30 words each (unmeasured per reply), every time. b saves those words but removes the chat copy that the guard option-labels-match-chat compares with the page, so a page and a chat that disagree would go unnoticed. a costs words; b costs a quiet mismatch.

shown.label: Page item plus option lines (triage's pick; main today)
One line, 'on the page, item N' (R18)

title: When a reply to you holds options, does chat carry one line ("on the page, item N"), or the page item plus its option lines?
why: Backlog-drain lane ledger in #3154; no past ruling settles it (triage read of rulings, steps and main's decisions 11:30 CST Nov 13).
